    eSSL Biometric Import

    Bring punches off eSSL / eTimeTrackLite devices into the punch log. Imported punches go through the same path as a web clock-in, so late marks, half days, overtime and the payroll muster all recompute from them.

    🗄️ Import from the eSSL database

    Pull punches straight out of the MySQL database eTimeTrackLite writes to — no file to carry across. A browser cannot open a database connection itself, so tools/essl-sync/server.js runs next to that database and hands the punches over.

    🗄️ Pull from the eSSL database

    Fetched punches land in the same preview as an uploaded file, and nothing is written until you import. Pulling a range you have already taken is safe — punches already in the log are skipped.

    📄 Or import a file by hand

    No connector, or a one-off correction: take the file off the device or out of the eSSL software and drop it in below. Both routes end in the same preview.

    📄 Device log file

    Download the log off the device or from the eSSL software — a tab-separated .dat / .txt with user ID, timestamp and state. No header row needed.

    📊 eTimeTrackLite export

    Reports → Device Logs / Attendance Register, exported to Excel or CSV. Column names vary by version, so every column is remappable below.

    🗄️ CSV from the database

    Where the HRMS cannot reach the eSSL machine over the network, tools/essl-sync/sync.js writes the same punches to a CSV you can carry across. MySQL Query above gives you the statement it runs.

    Device ID → employee

    An eSSL device knows people by their enrolment number. Map each to an employee once and every future import resolves on its own.

    Settings

    Every rule the system runs on, in one place. Each panel is the same one the screen it governs used to carry, so what you set here is what is enforced there.

    🗄️ Backend (Supabase)

    Without this the module keeps everything in this browser: fine to try, no good for real payroll. Point it at a Supabase project and identity, tenancy and entitlement move into Postgres, where row-level security decides what a query returns rather than the page deciding what to draw.

    Where to find these: Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → API Keys. Supabase renamed them, so depending on when your project was made you want either the Publishable key (sb_publishable_…) or, under Legacy API keys, the anon key (eyJ…). Either is fine. The Connect button at the top of the dashboard shows both the URL and the key together.

    These keys are meant to be public — row-level security is what protects the data, not the key. What must never go in a browser is the secret key (sb_secret_…, formerly service_role), which bypasses every policy. Run supabase/setup.sql first if you have not.

    Payroll components (formulas)

    For anything the CTC structure cannot express — a shift allowance, an attendance incentive, a recurring recovery. A component applies to everyone, one department or one person, every period, and is checked against real employees as you write it.

    ComponentTypeFormulaApplies toPreviewState

    Professional tax

    Each state's rule, written as a formula rather than buried in code, so it can be changed when the state changes it. The defaults are generated from the shipped slabs, so nothing moved when this was converted.

    StateFormulaAt 9k / 14k / 20k / 30k / 50kValid
